initial_scene: Front-facing seated humanoid behind a table. A small pale dumpling-shaped plush with a face rests inside an orange soft bowl at the robot's right side; the right hand is free and the left hand rests over the lap.

observed_sequence.action: Robot holds its initial seated posture with both hands low; dumpling plush remains in orange bowl.
Anatomical right arm reaches outward and down toward the dumpling plush in the orange bowl. Left hand stays at lap.
Right fingers settle around the plush and close, with adjustments while it remains in the bowl. Native frames 60, 100 and 152 show finger contact and grasp formation.
Right hand lifts the plush out of the bowl and holds it suspended forward and to the robot's right. The orange bowl stays on the table.
A person extends a palm-up hand from the foreground while robot maintains its grasp on the suspended plush.
Robot brings the plush forward and down toward the waiting palm, maintaining its right-hand grasp as the person raises and positions the receiving hand beneath it.

Plush settles into the person's hand; robot opens its right fingers to relinquish it. Person closes the receiving fingers around the plush and begins moving it away. Native frame 300 shows shared contact and frame 316 shows separation.
Person withdraws the plush toward foreground left and out of view; robot's now-empty right hand lifts away.
Robot retracts and lowers the empty right arm toward its lap. Left hand remains at lap and bowl is empty at final frame.

arm_hand_roles.right: Active throughout: reaches to bowl, grasps and lifts plush, carries it to the person's receiving palm, opens fingers for release, retracts empty hand.
arm_hand_roles.left: Inactive in the manipulation: remains open near the lap and provides no visible support, transfer, or bowl stabilization.
arm_hand_roles.person: Extends a palm-up receiving hand beneath the plush, supports it as robot opens fingers, then carries it away.
arm_hand_roles.coordination: One robot hand and the person's hand overlap in contact at transfer; robot lowers plush onto palm before opening fingers. No robot hand-to-hand transfer.

The reaching arm is continuously attached to the shoulder on the viewer's left of the front-facing chest, establishing anatomical right. The hand remaining at the lap attaches to the opposite shoulder and is anatomical left. Arm identity is followed continuously through all sheets and native transition views.
